title: 〜反面 / 〜半面
meaning: on the other side… / while (having a good side), it also has a bad side
simpleExplanation: 〜反面 means "on the flip side". You describe one side of something (usually the good side), then 反面 introduces the opposite side (usually a drawback). Both sides belong to the same thing: the same job, the same city, the same medicine. It is the natural way to say "X has this advantage, but also this disadvantage".
whenUsed: Written and formal spoken Japanese; essays, reviews, presentations. Both spellings 反面 and 半面 are seen; 反面 is more common on the JLPT. Typical uses: weighing pros and cons, describing personality (優しい反面、気が弱い).
formation: な-adjective + な / である + 反面
Second clause: the opposite side, usually a drawback (or a merit if the first side was negative)

parts.text: この仕事は給料がいい

diagram.translation: This job pays well, but on the other hand there is a lot of overtime.

examples.ja: この仕事は給料がいい反面、残業がとても多い。
examples.reading: このしごとはきゅうりょうがいいはんめん、ざんぎょうがとてもおおい。
examples.en: This job pays well, but on the other hand there is a lot of overtime.

examples.ja: 彼は優しい反面、気が弱いところがある。
examples.reading: かれはやさしいはんめん、きがよわいところがある。
examples.en: He is kind, but he can also be timid.

examples.ja: 都会は便利な反面、人間関係が薄いと言われる。
examples.reading: とかいはべんりなはんめん、にんげんかんけいがうすいといわれる。
examples.en: Cities are convenient, but human relationships are said to be shallow.

examples.ja: この薬はよく効く反面、副作用が心配だ。
examples.reading: このくすりはよくきくはんめん、ふくさようがしんぱいだ。
examples.en: This medicine works well, but the side effects are a concern.

examples.ja: 一人暮らしは自由である反面、寂しいときもある。
examples.reading: ひとりぐらしはじゆうであるはんめん、さびしいときもある。
examples.en: Living alone is free, but on the flip side there are lonely moments.
examples.note: な-adjective + である + 反面.

similarGrammar.difference: Also "on the other hand", but can describe two parallel activities or two different subjects. 反面 is strictly two sides of one thing.
"Instead of / in exchange for": a trade-off with a sense of compensation.
"Although": the expected result didn't follow. 反面 is a balanced pros-and-cons statement.
"Although", simultaneous contradictory state of one subject.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼女は会社で働く反面、家で子どもを育てている。
commonMistakes.right: 彼女は会社で働く一方、家で子どもを育てている。
commonMistakes.why: Two parallel activities are not opposite sides; use 一方. 反面 needs a merit/demerit contrast.

commonMistakes.wrong: この町は静か反面、不便だ。
commonMistakes.right: この町は静かな反面、不便だ。
commonMistakes.why: 静か is a な-adjective; な is needed before 反面.

commonMistakes.wrong: 値段が高い反面、質もよくない。
commonMistakes.right: 値段が高いばかりか、質もよくない。
commonMistakes.why: Both are drawbacks, pointing the same way. 反面 needs opposite sides; same-direction addition is ばかりか.

usageNotes: The first clause is often the good side, the second the bad side, but the reverse is fine: 給料は安い反面、休みが多い.
The same subject continues through both clauses; that is the key difference from 一方 and に対して.
反面 does not take で or に after it.
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, look for a merit and a demerit of the same thing. If the two clauses are parallel activities or different subjects, choose 一方 instead.
Distractors: 一方, かわりに, ものの, どころか. If both clauses point the same way, none of 反面/一方 fits; look for ばかりか.
Attachment: な-adjective + な + 反面, noun + である + 反面. Options such as 便利反面 are wrong.
